To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
anaerobic treatment of domestic sewage is an economically viable alternative to centralised treatment and reclamation, especially if it is combined with agricultural reuse.
anaerobic (pretreatment) can be an effective, cost-efficient and environmentally sound alternative for the reclamation of domestic sewage in urbanized (sub)tropical regions.

(i) anaerobic treatment is a cost-effective and reliable option for the pre-treatment of domestic sewage, (ii) the anaerobic effluent can be used for agricultural purposes and (iii) the produced biogases can be used as energy source for on-site applications, such as cooking or lighting, or for off-site applications, such e.g., the production of electricity or the production of biofuel for transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of cost-effective, sustainable and productive treatment and reuse systems for domestic wastewater in developing countries, based on anaerobic treatment.
the design and optimisation of anaerobic (pretreatment) processes for the decentralised treatment & reclamation of domestic sewage, stimulating its agricultural reuse.

(1) the development and application of innovative, cost-effective, decentralised anaerobic treatment and (2) the development of a cost-effective, integrated system for decentralised sewage treatment and agricultural reuse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of anaerobic pre-treatments in sewage reclamation is highly recommended.
anaerobic treatment of sewage is a feasible option to stimulate productive sewage reclamation in the (sub)tropics.
anaerobic treatment of domestic sewage is not only a feasible option, but also a promising and sustainable alternative for the reclamation of domestic sewage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anaerobic treatment can be a very cost-effective option for the reclamation of domestic sewage, particularly in the (sub)tropics.

anaerobic (bio)technology is an interesting option for sewage treatment in developing countries and that the anaerobic treatment of domestic wastewater is a feasible option to produce energy and/or nutrients for agricultural purposes.
anaerobic (pretreatment) is an attractive alternative for (pre-)treatments of domestic wastewater, particularly in the (sub)tropics, in which it is often used as irrigation water.
The main takeaway from our work is that

anaerobic treatment is a cost-effective and sustainable alternative for the decentralised treatment of domestic sewage, stimulating agricultural reuse, and thus contributing to the water security in urbanised areas.
anaerobic treatment of domestic sewage is a viable option for the decentralised and productive reclamation of domestic waste water.

anaerobic pre-treatments can play a major role in the reclamation of domestic sewage, especially in developing countries, but also in industrialised countries, in particular in those regions where water shortages are a major problem and where the sewerage and treatment facilities are insufficient.
